gap: No result ChatGPT got states a bench-measured delivered capacity for a 40,000 mAh laptop bank: ChargerLAB measured the AOHi Starship 40K at 121.6 Wh out at 20 V 5 A (100 W), 82.92% of its 146 Wh rating, and 116.52 Wh at 28 V 5 A (140 W), on a unit it weighed at 916.2 g.
standout_why: Compared against powerbanks.fyi/best/laptop-power-banks (cited): spec-sheet figures only, no delivered Wh, and no AOHi Starship 40K or Techsmarter entry. us.best-batteries.com high-capacity page: no measured capacity for any bank of 40,000 mAh or more. Macworld's roundup and its UGREEN 48,000 mAh review (in the results, not cited) do carry one named test: 1.8 recharges of a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro and 5% to 90% in an hour, so rivals hold the UGREEN half of the comparison. None holds a discharge test of the AOHi, and ChatGPT's own answer said its runtime figures were 'estimates, not measured results' and that it 'couldn't verify independent capacity tests'. Tom's Guide (cited) could not be compared: the fetch returned only navigation, so what it measured on the Cuktech 30 is unread. Standout is 2 rather than 3 because the two capacity figures come from different methods (electronic load vs counting laptop recharges) and Tom's Guide is unchecked.
decides: It replaces ChatGPT's estimated '100–125 Wh usable' with a measured figure, and it splits our two candidates on weight rather than capacity. The AOHi 40K delivered 121.6 Wh at 100 W (ChargerLAB); Macworld's 1.8 recharges of a 69.6 Wh MacBook Pro implies about 125 Wh from the UGREEN 48K. That is roughly the same laptop energy, but the AOHi weighed 916.2 g against 1.65 kg for the UGREEN as Macworld lists it. So the AOHi wins where the bank is carried and feeds one laptop at up to 132 W measured. The UGREEN wins on price ($118.99 against $143.20 through our link, both from the brief's tables, not re-read by me) and on feeding two or three laptops at once. ChargerLAB measured the AOHi dropping to 62 W + 32 W with two USB-C ports in use. The Cuktech 30, ChatGPT's pick, has no measured delivered capacity in any review I opened, so its lead rests on rated specs.

findings.label: Delivered energy at 100 W (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: 121.6 Wh at 20 V 5 A, 82.92% of the 146 Wh rating, 1 h 29 min runtime
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Constant-load discharge of one USB-C port from full to shut-off; efficiency is ChargerLAB's own division by the 146 Wh printed on the unit (29.2 V / 5,000 mAh).

findings.label: Delivered energy at 140 W (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: 116.52 Wh at 28 V 5 A, 79.81%, 1 h 3 min runtime
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Same test at the PD 3.1 maximum; about 5 Wh less comes out at 140 W than at 100 W.

findings.label: Delivered energy at lower loads (ChargerLAB)
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Phone-voltage output is the least efficient. The article's 5 V arithmetic is printed as 113.12/146 while the text says 113.21 Wh; the discrepancy is in the source.

findings.label: Weight and size as measured (ChargerLAB)
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: ChargerLAB's own scale and calipers. Teoh Yi Chie (Parka Blogs, July 3, 2024) gives 900 g.

findings.label: Output to a MacBook Pro, one port (ChargerLAB)
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Meter reading while charging a MacBook Pro over PD 3.1; the MacBook model was not captured in my reading.

findings.label: Output with several ports in use (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: Two USB-C: 62.37 W + 32.11 W. Three ports: 57.47 W + 34.54 W + 13.39 W (USB-A)
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Readings depend on what the attached devices asked for. Parka Blogs states the multi-port caps as 60 W, 60 W and 18 W. Either way, one laptop gets full speed and two do not.

findings.label: Recharge time and peak input (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: Full in 2 h 20 min; 50% in 32 min; 80% in 55 min; peak 135 W, above 130 W for the first 47 min
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Measured at 25 °C ambient with a 140 W source.

findings.label: Surface temperature at 140 W (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: 39.6 °C front, 36.2 °C back after 30 min at 28 V 5 A
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: Thermal camera reading at 25 °C ambient.

findings.label: Recharge time with a 100 W charger (Parka Blogs)
findings.value: 80% in one hour, 100% in 1.5 hours
findings.source_title: Review: AOHI Starship 40000 mAh laptop power bank (Teoh Yi Chie, July 3, 2024)
findings.note: Conflicts with ChargerLAB's 2 h 20 min at up to 135 W. A 100 W charger supplies at most 150 Wh in 1.5 h, which barely covers a 146 Wh pack before losses, so prefer ChargerLAB's logged figure.

findings.label: Laptop recharges obtained (Macworld)
findings.value: 1.8 recharges of a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro; 5% to 90% in one hour
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review: more power and ports than most (Simon Jary, Macworld, Jul 17, 2024)
findings.note: Method is counting recharges of the laptop, not an electronic-load discharge. The roundup (updated Nov 4, 2026) repeats it as 'Macworld Test Score: 180%'.

findings.label: Energy implied by Macworld's 1.8 recharges
findings.value: about 125 Wh into the laptop battery, about 82% of the 153.6 Wh rating
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (14-inch, 2023) - Tech Specs (Apple)
findings.note: My arithmetic: Apple gives the 14-inch 2023 (M2 Pro/Max) battery an actual rating of 69.6 Wh; 1.8 × 69.6 = 125.3 Wh; 125.3 / 153.6 = 81.6%. Assumes full 0–100% recharges, which Macworld does not specify. Not directly comparable with ChargerLAB's port-side figure.

findings.label: Rated capacity, weight and size as Macworld lists them
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review: more power and ports than most (Simon Jary, Macworld, Jul 17, 2024)
findings.note: 153.6 Wh / 48,000 mAh = 3.2 V, so the mAh figure is at LiFePO4 cell voltage. Per rated mAh it holds less energy than a 3.6–3.65 V bank: the AOHi's 40,000 mAh is 146 Wh.

findings.label: Weight as other named reviewers give it
findings.value: 4.1 lb (1.8 kg) per Android Central; 1.86 kg per Digital Camera World
findings.source_title: UGREEN 300W 48000mAh Power Bank review: The only power bank you'll ever need (Harish Jonnalagadda, Android Central, 24 June 2024)
findings.note: The Digital Camera World figure is from Paul Hatton's review of 5 July 2024 (https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/reviews/ugreen-300w-48000mah-power-bank-review, read 2026-11-26). Three reviewers give three weights, 1.65 to 1.86 kg, and none says it used a scale. Take the weight from UGREEN's own page.

findings.label: Recharge time (Macworld and Android Central)
findings.value: about 1.5 hours on the 140 W USB-C port (Macworld); full in just over 100 minutes (Android Central)
findings.source_title: UGREEN 300W 48000mAh Power Bank review: The only power bank you'll ever need (Harish Jonnalagadda, Android Central, 24 June 2024)
findings.note: The Macworld figure is from the review URL above. Paul Hatton (Digital Camera World) saw only 3–12 W of input and more than a day to refill, and suspected his cables. A 140 W PD 3.1 charger and a 5 A cable are needed for the fast figure.

findings.label: Phone-charging efficiency by the bank's own display (Android Central)
findings.value: around 55%: the display fell 8,500 mAh to charge a 4,500 mAh device and 10,500 mAh for a 5,500 mAh phone
findings.source_title: UGREEN 300W 48000mAh Power Bank review: The only power bank you'll ever need (Harish Jonnalagadda, Android Central, 24 June 2024)
findings.note: This is a ratio of mAh at different cell voltages (3.2 V in the bank, higher in a phone), read off the display, so it understates energy efficiency. It is not comparable with ChargerLAB's Wh figures.

findings.label: Ports used together (Android Central)
findings.value: Three USB-C at once: 100 W each, 300 W total; one port up to 140 W; all five ports: 130 W total
findings.source_title: UGREEN 300W 48000mAh Power Bank review: The only power bank you'll ever need (Harish Jonnalagadda, Android Central, 24 June 2024)
findings.note: Stated by the reviewer; the article does not show meter readings, so treat it as the rated split pending UGREEN's own page. Contrast with the AOHi's measured 62 W + 32 W on two ports.

findings.label: Weight carried per laptop watt-hour delivered (derived)
findings.value: AOHi 40K: about 7.5 g per delivered Wh. UGREEN 48K: about 13.2 g per delivered Wh. The AOHi weighs about 56% as much for about 3% less laptop energy
findings.source_title: Review of AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W Power Bank (ChargerLAB, June 3, 2025)
findings.note: My arithmetic: 916.2 g / 121.6 Wh = 7.5; 1,650 g / 125.3 Wh = 13.2; 916.2 / 1,650 = 55.5%; 121.6 / 125.3 = 97%. The UGREEN side uses Macworld's listed weight and the implied 125.3 Wh, and mixes two test methods, so present it as approximate.

findings.label: What named reviewers measured (The Gadgeteer)
findings.value: About 10 W into an HP laptop over USB-C; 22–24 W into a Surface tablet; 56 W total across five devices; 2.5 lb; refill in about 3.5 hours on a 40 W brick
findings.source_title: CUKTECH 30 40,000 mAh Power Bank and USB Hub review (Steve Holt, The Gadgeteer, March 30, 2025)
findings.note: No delivered-capacity test, and the reviewer says he could not test the MacBook Pro claim. 40 W for 3.5 h is 140 Wh, less than the 144 Wh rating, so the refill figure is loose. The 2.5 h refill at 140 W is Cuktech's claim, not a measurement.

findings.label: Recharge input observed (MacSources)
findings.value: 73–79 W input on a high-power adapter; iPhone 16 Pro drew about 16 W wired and about 10 W wireless by the bank's display
findings.source_title: CUKTECH 30 Power Bank 40000mAh REVIEW (Robyn, MacSources, March 14, 2025)
findings.note: Display readings with the bank starting at 31%; no laptop test and no capacity test.

findings.label: Price and rated capacity as Cult of Mac lists them
findings.value: 40,000 mAh (144 Wh); box price $179.99, body text says $150
findings.source_title: Cuktech 30 Power Bank review: Hefty but helpful on trips (David Snow, Cult of Mac, March 4, 2025)
findings.note: A March 2025 review price, not today's; the review gives no weight and no measured capacity. powerbanks.fyi lists 1,130 g from the spec sheet.
